# Audit scope: Rust contracts

<!-- Generated by scripts/audit-scope.mjs. Do not edit by hand: run `node scripts/audit-scope.mjs`. -->

This is the list of contract files and folders in the audit scope, with their sizes. `scripts/audit-scope.mjs` writes it from a git commit, so it can be regenerated for the frozen audit commit. Any contract change alters these counts, so regenerate it at the freeze and quote the numbers from that run.

## Snapshot

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `f51d301eb8b3de49b01463488e90eb2c8928d31f` (2026-11-25), the latest commit that changed a file in scope |
| `contracts/` tree | `fa2fb4863c926215303c0caa7b29d9510b1deb34` |
| Crates in scope | 9 |
| Code lines in scope | 9,073 |
| Unit tests in those crates | 524 |
| Code lines including test-only blocks inside source files | 9,433 |

To confirm a checkout matches this list, run `git rev-parse HEAD:contracts`: it prints the tree above. To regenerate for another commit or tag, run `node scripts/audit-scope.mjs --ref <tag>`; `--check` reports whether this file is current.

**How lines are counted.** A code line holds something other than whitespace and comments; blank lines, comment lines, and doc comments are left out. Test-only code is counted apart and is not in the scope total: the unit test files, and items behind a `cfg` that is false in a release build, such as `#[cfg(test)]` and `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testutils"))]`. Tools that do not read `cfg`, such as `cloc`, count the test-only blocks inside source files as code; the second line count above is that figure.

## Toolchain and dependencies

| | |
| --- | --- |
| soroban-sdk | `27.0.6` (crates.io), with the `experimental_spec_shaking_v2` feature |
| OpenZeppelin `stellar-contracts` | [github.com/OpenZeppelin/stellar-contracts](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/stellar-contracts) at rev `fbfde38`, commit `fbfde388e1b72afa93d6b1c922067879b20e81db` (from `Cargo.lock`). This is a git revision, not a tagged release |
| Rust toolchain | Pinned in [`rust-toolchain.toml`](../../rust-toolchain.toml) (below) |
| WASM target | `wasm32v1-none` |
| Stellar CLI | `28.0.0`, the version CI installs and checks by SHA-256 ([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml)) |

```toml
# The exact compiler every contract build uses. The WASM bytes, and so the hashes that upgrades
# approve, depend on it: rustc 1.95.0 with stellar-cli 28.0.0 is the toolchain that built every
# contract deployed so far. Change it only together with docker/wasm-build/Dockerfile and a new
# releases/hashes.json (docs/REPRODUCIBLE_BUILDS.md).
[toolchain]
channel = "1.95.0"
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]
targets = ["wasm32v1-none"]
profile = "minimal"
```

[`docs/OPENZEPPELIN_PIN.md`](../OPENZEPPELIN_PIN.md) records what the contracts use from this OpenZeppelin revision, how it differs from the nearby tags, why the project keeps it, and which OpenZeppelin audits cover it.

### Release profile

From the workspace [`Cargo.toml`](../../Cargo.toml). `overflow-checks = true` makes integer overflow abort in the WASM.

```toml
[profile.release]
opt-level = "z"
overflow-checks = true
debug = 0
strip = "symbols"
debug-assertions = false
panic = "abort"
codegen-units = 1
lto = true
```

## Build

From the repository root:

```bash
stellar contract build --locked
```

It builds every crate with a `cdylib` target into `target/wasm32v1-none/release/<crate>.wasm` and removes unused contract-spec entries from the WASM. A plain `cargo build` leaves those entries in, and the Token then exceeds the network's 128 KiB code limit. The WASM files in scope:

- `auction.wasm` from `contracts/auction`
- `governor.wasm` from `contracts/governor`
- `manager.wasm` from `contracts/manager`
- `marketplace.wasm` from `contracts/marketplace`
- `metadata.wasm` from `contracts/metadata`
- `minter.wasm` from `contracts/minter`
- `token.wasm` from `contracts/token`
- `treasury.wasm` from `contracts/treasury`

Run the tests after the build, because the integration tests load the built WASM:

```bash
cargo test --locked
```

### Reproducible build and published hashes

[`docs/REPRODUCIBLE_BUILDS.md`](../REPRODUCIBLE_BUILDS.md) describes the pinned build: the toolchain, the build image, the Stellar CLI, and the platform. Hashes are comparable only between builds made that way, because the same source gives different bytes on other platforms. It also explains how to rebuild a tag and check a hash, and records the checks made so far.

```bash
node scripts/build-wasm.mjs          # build this commit in the pinned container; print each contract's sha256
node scripts/verify-wasm.mjs <tag>   # rebuild a tag and compare it with the hashes the tag publishes
```

[`releases/hashes.json`](../../releases/hashes.json) records the sha256 and size of each contract from the container build, with the toolchain that built it. At this commit it does not describe the contracts in scope: it was last written at `da84863ea991`, and build inputs have changed since. Publish new hashes from the frozen commit (`node scripts/build-wasm.mjs --write-hashes`), commit them, and tag that commit.

### Test coverage

[`scripts/coverage.sh`](../../scripts/coverage.sh) (`pnpm contracts:coverage`) writes a `cargo llvm-cov` report of the contract crates. [`docs/COVERAGE.md`](../COVERAGE.md) gives the latest figures and what the report leaves out. The figures change with every contract change, so run it at the frozen commit.

## Out of scope

| Path | Why it is out of scope | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`contracts/e2e/`](../../contracts/e2e) | Integration tests (`dao-e2e`). They run the real contracts together in the in-memory host and are evidence for the audit, not deployed code. | 11 Rust files, 7,474 code lines, 118 tests |
| [`contracts/vote-adapter-mock/`](../../contracts/vote-adapter-mock) | A vote source whose admin sets any weight. It exists for tests and testnet and must never be approved on mainnet (see its README). | 3 Rust files, 222 code lines, 5 tests |
| The OpenZeppelin packages | Third-party code, listed above with the paths the contracts use. Whether the modules used are in scope is agreed in the scope letter. | |
| `soroban-sdk` and the Soroban host | Platform code, trusted as released. | |
| `apps/`, `packages/`, `db/` | The web app, the indexer, the generated bindings, and the SQL read model. They are not contract code; the app and indexer tier has its own [threat model](THREAT_MODEL.md). | |
| `scripts/`, `configs/`, `deploys/`, `releases/` | Deployment and operations tooling and records. | |
| `docs/`, `apps/docs/` | Documentation. It describes the contracts but is not part of them. | |
